title: Polpettone
subtitle: Italian meatloaf with boiled egg in the centre
excerpt: Polpettone is the Italian meatloaf: a mixture of minced beef and pork packed around a hard-boiled egg, braised in tomato sauce on the hob. Sliced at the table, each piece shows a cross-section of the egg in the centre. It is the kind of practical, unhurried dish that Italian home cooks have been making for generations.
sourceNotes: Italian home-cooking tradition. Polpettone with a whole egg at the centre is documented across Italian regional cookery books. Method drawn from Pellegrino Artusi, La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene (1891, public domain), and Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking (1992).

recipe.freezeNotes: Slice once cooled and freeze in portions. Thaw overnight and reheat in the tomato sauce.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to two days ahead. The polpettone slices more neatly when cold.

glossaryTerms.definition: Italian meatloaf; the name means 'large meatball'; the version with a hard-boiled egg in the centre is a classic of central and southern Italian home cooking.

content.text: Polpettone is a meatloaf shaped into a firm cylinder with a hard-boiled egg tucked in the centre. The word means 'large

'. It is braised slowly in tomato sauce rather than baked, which keeps it moist. When you slice it at the table, the egg in the cross-section makes it look far more impressive than the effort required.

Combine {{beef-mince}} of beef, {{pork-mince}} of pork, 2 raw eggs, {{breadcrumbs-dried}} of breadcrumbs, Parmesan, parsley, and garlic with salt. Mix until just combined. Flatten the mixture on a sheet of baking paper into a 30 x 20 cm rectangle. Lay the 2 hard-boiled eggs end to end in the centre. Roll the mixture tightly around the eggs into a firm cylinder. Seal the ends.

Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a wide casserole over medium-high heat. Brown the polpettone all over, about 8 minutes, turning gently. Remove. Cook the {{onion}} onion in the pan for 4 minutes. Add {{dry-white-wine}} of wine and let it reduce by half. Add the tomatoes. Return the polpettone to the sauce. Cover and simmer over low heat for 45 minutes, turning once halfway.
Rest for 5 minutes. Slice at the table and serve with the sauce spooned over.

items.cause: Mixture too loose, or not browned long enough to form a crust before turning.
items.fix: Chill the formed log for 20 minutes before cooking. Brown each side well before attempting to turn it.

items.symptom: Eggs are not centred in the slice
items.cause: Eggs placed off-centre in the rectangle, or the log was rolled unevenly.
items.fix: Lay the eggs end to end precisely in the middle of the meat rectangle. Roll tightly and evenly.

content.text: Polpettone is practical Italian home cooking: cheap, unfussy, and more satisfying than it looks. The version with a boiled egg in the centre is the Sunday version, made when there is no occasion to mark but when dinner should feel a little special. Artusi calls it a dish of the people, made wherever there is minced meat to hand.
